title: OpenBISmantic

narrative_arc.enters_knowing: They have an openBIS ELN/LIMS instance and want to expose it as Linked Data.
narrative_arc.leaves_knowing: What OpenBISmantic provides, how content negotiation works, the RO-Crate export feature, deployment options, limitations.
steps: Status badge: Demonstrator — no active public deployment
What OpenBISmantic does — wraps openBIS with FastAPI, all entities as resolvable RDF IRIs via permIds
Content negotiation — same URL, different Accept header → different RDF format (inline curl pair)
openBIS hierarchy mapped to RDF: Space → Project → Collection → Object → Dataset
RO-Crate export — /export_bundle endpoint for portable archival
Deployment options: full stack (includes openBIS) vs. API-only (points at existing openBIS)
Downstream: RO-Crate ZIP → RDFConverter for semantic mapping

inline_assets_required.description: Content negotiation curl pair: same URL, Accept: application/ld+json vs Accept: application/x-turtle. Use placeholder URL since no public deployment. Label: # replace with your OpenBISmantic URL
Deployment curl: git clone + docker compose up for full-stack deployment.

walkthrough_requirements.step: No public deployment — use placeholder URLs
walkthrough_requirements.note: All curl examples use placeholder https://your-openbismantic.example.org. Label clearly.

quality_gate: Status badge: Demonstrator — no active public deployment
Content negotiation curl example present (two Accept headers for same URL)
Two deployment modes documented (full stack vs. API-only)
Required env vars listed (OPENBIS_URL, BASE_URL, ADMIN_PASS)
notes: Page is partial. openbismantic-service.json has full content. No public deployment — all curls use placeholder. Requires openBIS 20.10+ server (PyBIS auth requirement). Output uses Schema.org/DCAT/PROV-O — domain-specific mapping needs downstream YARRRML via RDFConverter.

primary.name: Domain Scientist
knows: Their scientific domain deeply (materials science, microscopy, lab procedures)
Measurement concepts and experimental workflows they consider universal
Domain-specific tools (OMERO, ELN systems, instrument software)
does_not_know: Ontology terms like PMDCO, CHAMEO, EMMO even if these describe their own work
How ontologies model domain concepts — that this modeling discipline exists at all
SPARQL, RDF, or any semantic technology
primary.goal: Upload their data, trigger the pipeline, and use or export FAIR-compliant results.
primary.key_gap: Double gap: (1) no semantic web knowledge whatsoever, and (2) domain experts frequently assume their concepts are universal common knowledge when they are not — documentation must not assume shared domain vocabulary and must explain what gets modeled and why, not just how.

secondary.name: Data Engineer
secondary.goal: Connect data sources, author mappings, and query transformation results.
